mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds +1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressures and input costs, compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for four consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered instances, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both GDPC1 and HOUST above their respective 6-month moving averages signals strengthening housing demand and broader economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically above zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL below their 12-month averages for three consecutive months signals a coordinated easing in monetary policy and inflation, which lowers real discount rates and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 12-month MA and CPIAUCSL < 12-month MA for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly above zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent fall in PAYEMS below its 12-month moving average by more than 1% for five consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between RSAFS and GDPC1 at the monthly frequency over a 12-month rolling window implies that rising household savings coincide with expanding economic activity, which supports higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between RSAFS and GDPC1 turns negative for any consecutive 12-month window, or S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly above zero when the correlation is positive at 95% confidence.
